_doc: Single source of the channel copy shown by the CLI, Atlas Desktop and the website. The `promise` strings must appear verbatim in docs/versioning.md (a test in atlas-core enforces it). Edit both together.
stage_note: Atlas is in alpha. Every channel, including Stable, can have rough edges and breaking changes until the first release that meets the general availability criteria in the versioning policy.

channels.label: Stable
channels.promise: The default. Only builds that already ran as a beta, with nothing changed since but the version number.
channels.cadence: When a soaked beta is promoted, usually every few weeks.
channels.audience: Everyone, and anyone who uses Atlas for real work.
channels.switch_to: You move to the next Stable release that is newer than the version you run. Atlas never installs an older build by itself.
channels.alpha_era_note: While Atlas is in alpha, Stable means soaked through alpha and beta, not finished.

channels.label: Beta
channels.promise: Feature-complete builds that are being soaked before they become Stable. Only fixes land between betas.
channels.risk_label: Mostly works; a bug can slip through
channels.cadence: A new beta about every one to two weeks while a release is soaking.
channels.audience: People who want next release's features a few weeks early and will report what breaks.
channels.switch_to: You get the newest beta or release candidate, and Stable as soon as it is newer. Going back to Stable later waits for a Stable newer than your build, or you can reinstall Stable explicitly.

channels.label: Alpha
channels.promise: Fresh builds cut straight from main, with little soak. Features can be unfinished and behavior can change between builds.
channels.risk_label: Expect rough edges and breaking changes
channels.cadence: Whenever the maintainer cuts one, often several times a week.
channels.audience: Contributors and testers who accept breakage in exchange for the newest work.
channels.switch_to: You get the newest build of any channel, so a settings or config change may not be readable by an older Atlas. Going back to Beta or Stable later waits for a newer build there, or you can reinstall it explicitly.
